request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information: 
The patient is a 26-year-old female who was referred to the Medical Oncology department for surgical resection of multiple hepatic metastases. The patient had previously undergone a subtotal gastrectomy for an epithelioid GIST variant localised to the muscularis propia and was diagnosed with pT1pN0 (0/1) with a high mitotic rate - stage II. The patient was found to be positive for CD117 (KIT) and DOG1. The mutational analysis revealed that the tumor was KIT and PDGFRα WT.

Hospital Course:
The patient underwent complete resection of the hepatic metastases and subsequent image studies confirmed no evidence of disease. Adjuvant treatment with imatinib was not delivered due to complete resection of WT GIST. 

Family History:
The patient has a 19-year-old healthy brother. There is no significant family history of diseases; however, the patient's paternal grandparent was diagnosed with a pituitary adenoma at age 30 and died at age 52.

Genetic Testing:
Based on the patient's molecular features of diagnosed GIST, age at presentation and apparently irrelevant family history, SDHx germline analysis was performed in peripheral blood. No further details of the genetic test were provided.

Follow-Up:
The patient is currently 26 years of age and has no evidence of active disease. Additional follow-up appointments may be required as per the physician's recommendation. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Instructions:
The patient has been advised to follow up with her physician as required and to notify medical professionals of any adverse symptoms. No further specific discharge instructions were provided.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: C78**

The episode was admitted for surgical resection of multiple hepatic metastases, which is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. The metastases are secondary malignant neoplasm of the liver (C78.7). The original gastric GIST had already been treated by subtotal gastrectomy, so it is not the reason for this episode.
